final_candidates.decision_summary: K119 is the catalytic PLP-binding lysine; removing it abolishes Schiff-base formation and CBS activity. Strongest damaging signal (0.987) and low evolutionary tolerance support complete LOF.
Charge reversal at the same catalytic lysine (0.974 damaging) provides an independent route to eliminate PLP binding and catalysis. Conserved position with low mutant frequency.
C52 is the N-terminal heme axial ligand; its loss disrupts heme-dependent CBS structure/function, with a high damaging score (0.951). Slight evolutionary tolerance at this site tempers confidence.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 is anchored by mechanistically essential residues with concordant damaging predictions; extra tool rounds would not reorder them.

history.rationale: Lys119 is the conserved catalytic residue that covalently binds the PLP cofactor; alanine substitution should abolish Schiff-base formation and enzyme activity.
K119 is the catalytic PLP-binding lysine of CBS; replacing it with Ala abolishes Schiff-base formation and enzyme activity. Classic, well-characterized LOF mutation.
Highest damaging signal (alphamissense 0.987) at a conserved position (low mutant frequency 0.056); K119 is the PLP-binding catalytic lysine, so substitution directly abolishes CBS activity.
Charge-reversing substitution of the PLP-binding lysine should strongly disrupt cofactor anchoring and catalysis.
Charge reversal at the catalytic lysine should fully destroy PLP cofactor binding while remaining structurally tolerated.
Charge-reversal at the same catalytic PLP-lysine gives 0.974 damaging score and low evolutionary tolerance (0.125), a strong independent LOF route.
Cys52 is the proximal heme ligand in the N-terminal heme domain; its loss perturbs the redox-sensing heme cofactor and strongly destabilizes catalytic function.
C52 lies in the N-terminal heme-binding CXXC motif; mutation disrupts heme coordination and reduces activity, though some residual activity is possible.
Strong damaging score 0.951; C52 is the N-terminal heme axial ligand so loss disrupts heme-dependent CBS function. MSA Ala frequency 0.218 tempers confidence slightly, so ranked below the K119 pair.
A known pathogenic CBS variant in the catalytic core associated with homocystinuria and severely reduced activity.
R125 sits in the catalytic core near the PLP site; a polar-for-basic swap may perturb substrate/cofactor binding.
Benign phenotype prediction (0.153); inconsistent with abolishing activity.

rejection.reason: Benign phenotype prediction (0.153); inconsistent with abolishing activity.

history.rationale: Classic pathogenic CBS mutation in the catalytic domain that markedly reduces enzyme activity in homocystinuria patients.
G307 is in the highly conserved catalytic-domain glycine-rich loop (GTGGT motif); Gly-to-Ser disrupts the active-site architecture and is a known pathogenic-class substitution.
Damaging score 0.828 with low mutant frequency (0.074) at a conserved catalytic-core glycine; promoted to rank 4 as the leading backup.
The most common CBS pathogenic allele; a destabilizing active-site-adjacent substitution that lowers residual activity and folding efficiency.
I278T is the most common homocystinuria-causing CBS allele; well-validated severe LOF though folding/misfolding-mediated.
Alphamissense classifies benign (0.159) despite conservation; does not serve the LOF objective.

rejection.reason: Alphamissense classifies benign (0.159) despite conservation; does not serve the LOF objective.

history.rationale: Recurrent pathogenic substitution in the substrate-binding/catalytic region associated with loss of CBS activity.
R336C is a reported pathogenic CBS variant likely impairing catalysis.
Only ambiguous damaging score (0.423) and MSA coverage too low (app 0.14) to support a LOF claim.

rejection.reason: Only ambiguous damaging score (0.423) and MSA coverage too low (app 0.14) to support a LOF claim.

history.rationale: Documented homocystinuria-causing variant near the PLP-binding pocket with substantially reduced catalytic activity.
T191M is a known pathogenic CBS mutation affecting the active site; plausible strong LOF.
Moderately damaging (0.716) at a conserved site; kept as depth candidate but clearly below the top four.
